# Vendored secret-detection rules

## `gitleaks.toml`

A verbatim copy of the default gitleaks configuration.

- Source: <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/master/config/gitleaks.toml>
- Fetched: 2026-08-29
- Upstream `minVersion`: v8.25.0

gitleaks is distributed under the MIT License, Copyright (c) 2019 Zachary Rice.
The rules in `gitleaks.toml` are reproduced from its default configuration under
that licence; see <https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/blob/master/LICENSE>.

**Do not edit this file.** It is vendored unmodified so that the copy here can
be diffed against upstream. To sync:

```
uv run python tools/sync_gitleaks_rules.py
```

That downloads the upstream file and replaces `gitleaks.toml` wholesale — the
only part of this project allowed to touch the network. `gate.py` then loads it
at import and compiles each rule's regex; **rules that do not compile under the
running interpreter are skipped at load time** (logged at DEBUG with the rule
id) rather than failing the import. The patterns are written for Go's RE2, so a
couple of dozen use constructs Python's `re` rejects, and which ones depends on
the interpreter version — `\z` is only valid from Python 3.14 on.

> **Which rules are active depends on the running Python version, so the same
> content can be rejected on one machine and accepted on another sharing the
> same store.** Skipping happens at load time, per interpreter: 3.14 loads 198
> of the 222 upstream rules, 3.12 loads 195. The four rules using `\z`
> (`curl-auth-header`, `curl-auth-user`, `openshift-user-token`,
> `sentry-org-token`) are the difference — `curl-auth-header` is skipped on both
> for a separate reason, so the net gain on 3.14 is three rules. A newer
> interpreter therefore gates strictly more content than an older one; it never
> gates less. Pin the interpreter if uniform verdicts across a shared store
> matter.

### Divergences from gitleaks' own behaviour

- Allowlists and stopwords are not applied; these rules therefore fire more
  often here than upstream gitleaks would.
- Entropy rejects at `>= threshold`; upstream skips at `<= threshold`, so this
  gate is stricter by the boundary case.
- Path-only rules (no `regex`) are ignored — memriver gates content, not files.

## `memriver.toml`

memriver's own rules, written in the same `[[rules]]` schema and loaded first.
Not vendored, not from upstream, and covered by this repository's own licence.
